question: m01
q: Are real wages going up? Compare wage growth from the ABS Wage Price Index with inflation.

transcript.answer:
**No. Real wages are going down again.** Wages grew 3.2% in the year to the June quarter 2026, while prices rose about 4%. That means real wages fell by about 0.6–0.8 percentage points, and it's the third quarter in a row they've gone backwards. They had been rising from late 2023 through 2025.

**Wages vs. prices, change over the year**

| Quarter | Wage growth (WPI) | Inflation (CPI) | Real wage change |
|---|---|---|---|
| Mar 2023 | 3.7% | 7.0% | −3.3 pts |
| Jun 2023 | 3.7% | 6.0% | −2.3 |
| Sep 2023 | 4.0% | 5.4% | −1.4 |
| Dec 2023 | 4.3% | 4.1% | +0.2 |
| Mar 2024 | 4.0% | 3.6% | +0.4 |
| Jun 2024 | 4.1% | 3.8% | +0.3 |
| Sep 2024 | 3.6% | 2.8% | +0.8 |
| Dec 2024 | 3.2% | 2.4% | +0.8 |
| Mar 2025 | 3.5% | 2.4% | +1.1 |
| Jun 2025 | 3.4% | 2.1% | **+1.3** (best result) |
| Sep 2025 | 3.3% | 3.2% | +0.1 |
| Dec 2025 | 3.4% | ~3.7%* | about −0.3 |
| Mar 2026 | 3.2% | ~4.0%* | about −0.8 |
| Jun 2026 | 3.2% | ~4.0%* | about −0.8 |

*The ABS stopped publishing the quarterly CPI after September 2025, so these are averages of the three monthly inflation figures in each quarter. If you use only the last month of each quarter instead, inflation was 3.8% (Dec), 4.6% (Mar) and 3.8% (Jun), which gives real wage changes of −0.4, −1.4 and −0.6 points.

**What happened:**
- **2023: falling.** Prices were rising 5–7% a year and wages only about 4%.
- **Late 2023 to Sep 2025: rising.** Inflation came down faster than wage growth, so wages gained on prices for eight straight quarters. The gap peaked at +1.3 points in June 2025.
- **Late 2025 onwards: falling again.** Inflation picked up from 1.9% in June 2025 to 3.8% by October 2025 and peaked at 4.6% in March 2026. Meanwhile wage growth eased from about 3.4% to 3.2%.

**Looking ahead:** Inflation was 4.0% in the year to August 2026, the latest monthly figure. September quarter wage figures haven't been released yet, but unless wage growth jumps well above its recent 3.2–3.4% range, real wages are still likely shrinking.

**How the figures are measured:** Wages are the ABS Wage Price Index (hourly pay excluding bonuses, all industries, private and public sector, seasonally adjusted). Prices are the ABS all-groups CPI for Australia. The WPI tracks pay rates for the same jobs over time, so it doesn't capture people getting promotions, changing jobs or working different hours.
